quests.instruction: Which part of a bus, train, or airplane is meant for passengers to sit on during a trip?
quests.hint: You will find rows of them, all facing the same way.
quests.explanation: Seats let passengers rest safely during a journey. Cars and planes also have seat belts to keep people in place.
quests.funFact: Some trains have seats that can turn to face the direction the train is travelling.

quests.instruction: Which part helps a driver see the traffic behind without turning around?
quests.hint: It is a shiny surface mounted outside or inside the car.
quests.explanation: Mirrors show drivers what is behind and beside them. Drivers check them before turning, stopping, or changing lanes.
quests.funFact: Large trucks and buses have extra mirrors because they have bigger blind spots.

quests.instruction: Which small device on a bicycle rings to tell people you are coming?
quests.hint: Press it with your thumb and it makes a ringing sound.
quests.explanation: A bicycle bell is a polite warning. A quick ring tells walkers and other riders that you are close.
quests.funFact: In some countries, bicycles must have a bell by law.

quests.instruction: Which flashing light on top of an emergency vehicle warns drivers to make way?
quests.hint: It spins or flashes brightly in red, blue, or other colours.
quests.explanation: Emergency lights get attention quickly, even in daylight and traffic. When drivers see them, they should stay calm and let the emergency vehicle pass safely.
quests.funFact: Different countries and services use blue, red, or amber lights for emergencies.

quests.instruction: Which feature lets a driver see the road ahead after dark?
quests.hint: It shines forward and also helps other people notice the vehicle.
quests.explanation: Headlights light up the road and show other people that a vehicle is coming. They are used in the dark, in fog, and in heavy rain.
quests.funFact: Bicycle lights are usually white at the front and red at the back.

quests.instruction: Which tool has a needle that always points north to help travellers find direction?
quests.hint: Its needle is magnetic and swings until it settles.
quests.explanation: A compass uses a magnetic needle that points north. Sailors, pilots, and hikers use it with a map to find their way.
quests.funFact: Sailors were using compasses hundreds of years ago, long before modern navigation.

quests.instruction: Which of these has the most wheels?
quests.hint: Very heavy loads need many wheels to share the weight.
quests.explanation: A long truck with a trailer has many wheels to share the weight of its load. A car has four wheels and a bicycle has two.
quests.funFact: Some special trucks that carry huge machines have dozens of wheels.

quests.instruction: Which small two-wheeler has a flat place for your feet and a body that covers the engine?
quests.hint: You sit upright and step through the frame instead of swinging a leg over.
quests.explanation: A motor scooter is a small, light two-wheeler used for short trips in towns. Its open frame makes it easy to get on and off.
quests.funFact: Scooters are popular in busy cities because they are easy to park.

quests.instruction: Which battery-powered seat on wheels helps someone who finds walking tiring or difficult to get around?
quests.hint: A small control lets the rider drive without pushing the wheels by hand.
quests.explanation: A motorised wheelchair has an electric motor, so the user can travel without using their arms to push. It helps people get to school, shops, and parks.
quests.funFact: Many buses and trains now have ramps or lifts so wheelchair users can get on board.

quests.instruction: Which tall machine lifts heavy beams high into the air at a building site?
quests.hint: It has a long arm that reaches up, and a hook that swings loads.
quests.explanation: A crane lifts and moves heavy materials that people could never carry by hand. Tall cranes help build skyscrapers floor by floor.
quests.funFact: Tower cranes are often built higher as a building rises, so they can keep reaching the top.

quests.instruction: Which animal, with a hump on its back, has long carried people and goods across hot deserts?
quests.hint: It can travel a long way without a drink.
quests.explanation: Camels are strong and can travel far in hot, dry places. For many centuries, lines of camels carried people and goods across deserts.
quests.funFact: A camel's hump stores fat, not water.

quests.instruction: Which animal pulls a carriage or cart steered with reins?
quests.hint: The driver holds long straps to guide it.
quests.explanation: Horses are strong and fast. Before engines, they pulled carts, carriages, and ploughs, and carried riders over long distances.
quests.funFact: We still measure engine power in 'horsepower'.

quests.instruction: Which cloth canopy opens to slow someone down when they fall from an aircraft?
quests.hint: It fills with air, a bit like a very wide umbrella.
quests.explanation: A parachute catches air and makes a falling person drop slowly, so they can land safely. Pilots and skydivers use them.
quests.funFact: Parachutes also slow down spacecraft and heavy cargo as they return to the ground.

quests.instruction: Which machine circles Earth high above and helps phone maps know where you are?
quests.hint: It flies far above the clouds with no pilot inside.
quests.explanation: Navigation satellites send signals down to Earth. A phone uses signals from several satellites to work out where it is on the map.
quests.funFact: GPS satellites orbit about 20,000 kilometres above Earth.

quests.instruction: Which is a single railway carriage where passengers sit, joined to others in a line?
quests.hint: Many of these are linked together behind the front of the train.
quests.explanation: A carriage, or railway car, is where passengers sit or goods are carried. Many carriages are joined together to make a train.
quests.funFact: Some long freight trains have more than a hundred wagons.

quests.instruction: Which footwear has wheels so you can glide along smooth pavement?
quests.hint: Four small wheels sit under each boot.
quests.explanation: Roller skates have wheels fitted under boots. Skaters push sideways with their feet and glide along smooth, flat ground.
quests.funFact: The first roller skates were invented in the 1700s.

quests.instruction: Which footwear has a thin metal blade for gliding over ice?
quests.hint: Wheels would be useless here. It glides on a sharp edge.
quests.explanation: Ice skates have thin blades that glide over the slippery surface of ice. Skaters push with one blade at a time.
quests.funFact: In cold countries, people have skated across frozen lakes and canals as a way to travel for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: Which long, narrow pair of boards lets someone glide down a snowy slope?
quests.hint: They spread your weight over the snow so you do not sink in.
quests.explanation: Skis are long and flat, so they spread weight and slide easily over snow. Skiers use poles to push themselves along.
quests.funFact: Skis were first used long ago to travel across snowy lands, well before they became a sport.

quests.instruction: Which symbol is often shown at charging points for electric vehicles?
quests.hint: Look for a zigzag shape.
quests.explanation: The lightning symbol stands for electricity. Electric vehicles plug in to fill up on power instead of filling a fuel tank.
quests.funFact: Many electric trains get their power from wires above, or from a special rail beside the track.

quests.instruction: Which plug and cable connect an electric car to a power supply so it can charge?
quests.hint: Think of how you charge a phone from the wall.
quests.explanation: Electric cars charge by plugging a cable into a power source. Charging fills the car's battery with electricity so it can drive again.
quests.funFact: Some electric vehicles can be charged at home overnight.

quests.instruction: Which bus gets its power from two wires strung above the street?
quests.hint: Two long poles on its roof touch wires overhead.
quests.explanation: A trolleybus is an electric bus with rubber tyres. Poles on its roof pick up electricity from wires above the road.
quests.funFact: Trolleybuses are quieter than diesel buses, and some cities have used them for close to a hundred years.

quests.instruction: Which round red sign with a white bar tells drivers they cannot go this way?
quests.hint: You often see it at the end of a one-way street.
quests.explanation: A no-entry sign means vehicles may not drive into the road from this direction. It helps stop drivers from meeting head-on.
quests.funFact: Red is used on many warning and stop signs because it is easy to notice.

quests.instruction: Which sign tells people on foot that they are not allowed to walk here?
quests.hint: A walking figure is crossed out.
quests.explanation: Some roads, like fast highways and tunnels, are not safe for walkers. The sign tells pedestrians to find another way.
quests.funFact: Many motorways do not allow walkers or bicycles because the traffic moves so fast.

quests.instruction: Which yellow triangle sign tells drivers to take extra care because of something ahead?
quests.hint: It is a triangle with a mark inside.
quests.explanation: A warning sign shows that something unusual is ahead, like a sharp bend or a slippery road. Drivers should slow down and be ready.
quests.funFact: In many countries, warning signs are triangles, which makes them look different from round signs that give instructions.

quests.instruction: Which bright energy source from the sky can power the panels on a solar car?
quests.hint: It rises each morning and sets each evening.
quests.explanation: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. Some small cars, boats, and charging stations use this clean power.
quests.funFact: Solar cars race across Australia in the World Solar Challenge.

quests.instruction: Long ago, people made boats by hollowing out which natural material?
quests.hint: Choose the material that floats on a pond.
quests.explanation: A hollowed-out log floats and can carry a person across water. These dugout canoes are among the oldest boats ever found.
quests.funFact: The Pesse canoe, found in the Netherlands, is about 10,000 years old.

quests.instruction: Which warning icon shows that an electric vehicle's battery is almost empty?
quests.hint: The battery picture has only a sliver of colour left.
quests.explanation: When the battery is low, the driver needs to find a charging point soon. Planning stops helps electric vehicles finish longer trips.
quests.funFact: Many electric cars show on their screens where the nearest charging points are.

quests.instruction: Which tall car with big tyres is built for bumpy roads and rough tracks?
quests.hint: Its raised body helps it clear rocks and ruts.
quests.explanation: An SUV or off-road vehicle sits higher off the ground and has strong tyres. It handles rough surfaces better than a low car.
quests.funFact: Many of these vehicles can drive with all four wheels at once, which helps them grip mud and snow.

quests.instruction: Which tool do mechanics use to tighten the nuts and bolts on a vehicle?
quests.hint: It grips the head of a bolt so you can turn it.
quests.explanation: A spanner, or wrench, lets mechanics turn bolts tight. Regular check-ups help keep vehicles safe on the road.
quests.funFact: Formula 1 pit crews can change all four tyres in under three seconds.

quests.instruction: In the United States, which vehicle is painted bright yellow to carry children to school?
quests.hint: It has flashing lights and a stop sign that swings out.
quests.explanation: Yellow school buses are easy to spot. Other drivers know to be extra careful around them, especially when children are getting on or off.
quests.funFact: The standard school-bus yellow was chosen in the USA in 1939.
